title: ExxonMobil Holdings (XOM) Stock: Shares Slide 1.62% as Company Unveils $3B Debt Buyback Results - Blockonomi
content: ExxonMobil Holdings (XOM) shares declined 1.62% to $157.40, losing $2.59 as selling pressure erased earlier gains. The stock briefly approached $161.70 before retreating toward intraday lows during the trading session. Meanwhile, ExxonMobil announced results from its $3 billion debt repurchase program involving four outstanding note series. ExxonMobil disclosed the pricing terms and final tender results for debt repurchases conducted through two subsidiaries. Pioneer Natural Resources Company and Exxon Mobil Corporation managed separate cash offers covering their respective outstanding notes. The companies launched the offers on November 16, 2026, with a combined repurchase limit of $3 billion. However, total eligible submissions remained below the maximum amount, allowing both subsidiaries to accept every valid tender. Consequently, neither company needed to reduce accepted amounts through proportional allocations across the four note series. The accepted principal totaled approximately $1.76 billion, covering debt obligations with maturities ranging from 2030 through 2040. The transaction includes two Pioneer note series and two Exxon note series with different interest rates. Pioneer offered to repurchase its 1.900% senior notes due 2030 and 2.150% senior notes due 2031. Exxon targeted its 3.482% notes due 2030 and 4.227% notes due 2040 under separate offers. Pioneer accepted $128.68 million in notes due 2030 and $97.79 million in notes due 2031. The company established consideration of $896.86 and $892.94 per $1,000 principal amount for those respective securities. Both series carried pricing spreads of 22 and 30 basis points above their reference Treasury yields. Exxon accepted approximately $705.41 million of its 3.482% notes maturing in 2030. The company also accepted $832.68 million of its 4.227% notes scheduled to mature in 2040. Their respective repurchase prices reached $957.85 and $872.59 per $1,000 principal amount, excluding accrued interest. The companies calculated these prices using reference Treasury yields and predetermined spreads for each security. Furthermore, both subsidiaries will pay accrued interest through the day preceding the settlement date. The repurchases reduce outstanding debt principal while requiring cash payments according to the announced tender terms. ExxonMobil shares fell $2.59 during the session, marking a 1.62% decline to $157.40. Earlier buying briefly lifted the stock toward $161.70 before sustained selling reversed those gains. Consequently, XOM finished the reported trading period near its intraday lows despite the company’s debt announcement. The debt repurchases follow ExxonMobil’s acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources, which expanded its Permian Basin operations. That acquisition also brought Pioneer’s existing debt obligations into ExxonMobil’s broader corporate structure. The latest tender program addresses selected outstanding securities rather than the company’s entire debt portfolio. The announced results confirm full acceptance of valid tenders without exceeding the established $3 billion ceiling. Additionally, the final accepted amount leaves approximately $1.24 billion below the maximum authorized principal amount. XOM’s share decline accompanied the announcement, although the reported trading figures do not establish its underlying cause. title: ExxonMobil's $4B Kizomba Redevelopment: Can It Drive Earnings Growth? - TradingView
content: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM and its partners are advancing an estimated $4 billion redevelopment of Angola’s offshore Kizomba A and B fields following a final investment decision, according to Angola's National Oil, Gas and Biofuels Agency (“ANPG”). The investment underscores ExxonMobil’s focus on expanding resource development and sustaining production in Angola. The extension of Block 15’s production sharing agreement through 2037 provides a longer operating horizon for the project. For XOM, the redevelopment offers an opportunity to sustain oil sales and boost upstream earnings. The partners announced a hydrocarbon discovery at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 exploration well, marking Block 15’s 21st discovery and its second this year. The well encountered about 65.4 meters of hydrocarbon-bearing sandstone with favorable reservoir properties, highlighting the block’s resource potential. Subject to successful evaluation and development, the discovery provides another avenue for future production and cash generation. The Angola investment aligns with the energy major’s strategy to strengthen earnings through disciplined capital allocation, technology and operating efficiency, as outlined in its third-quarter 2026 results. By extending the productive lives of established fields, the Kizomba redevelopment provides a path to strengthen the contribution from XOM’s existing upstream portfolio. Successful execution and commercial development of additional resources will support earnings growth. TTE & COP Add Production to Support Earnings Growth Like ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies SE TTE and ConocoPhillips COP are advancing upstream developments that expand production and support earnings potential. TotalEnergies highlighted the ramp-up of its Ratawi development in Iraq during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, with production exceeding 100,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (Boe/d). TotalEnergies expected the initial oil development phase to reach 120,000 Boe/d by November, while construction continued toward expansion. For TTE, rising production adds sales volume, while low operating costs improve the opportunity to translate additional output into earnings and cash generation. On the third quarter of 2026 earnings call, ConocoPhillips reported that a new Surmont production pad in Canada started operating ahead of schedule and under budget. The company expects the additional production to support Canadian growth in 2027, complementing development in the Lower 48. COP’s preliminary 2027 outlook calls for low-single-digit underlying production growth, modestly lower capital spending and lower unit operating costs, a combination that supports higher margins.
